headline: Human rights court says a 46-nation call on deportations will not set its course
deck: Denmark's new deportation rules would have no effect if the court does not change course, a law professor says.
standard: Mattias Guyomar, president of the European Court of Human Rights, said in a speech last week that a declaration by the 46 countries behind the court 'is not a roadmap for the court's work'. The countries, members of the Council of Europe, signed it in Chisinau, Moldova's capital, in May, seeking more freedom to deport foreign criminals.

Mette Frederiksen, the prime minister, led the push, and her government's deportation reform assumes the court will change its practice over time. 'If it turns out that the court does not change course, the new Danish rules will have no effect,' Jens Elo Rytter, professor of constitutional law at the University of Copenhagen, tells Ritzau.
short: Mattias Guyomar, president of the European Court of Human Rights, said last week that a declaration by the 46 countries behind the court on deporting foreign criminals 'is not a roadmap for the court's work'. Jens Elo Rytter, professor of constitutional law at the University of Copenhagen, tells Ritzau that if the court does not change course, Denmark's new deportation rules will have no effect.
